catalog_quote: Vowel length and stress are not contrastive. Preliminary observations would suggest primary stress is placed on the first syllable.7 Understanding how stress placement is affected by verbal morphology, and how stress affects the length of syllables (both stressed and unstressed), requires further research. ... [fn. 7] Klaiman (1987:499) notes a similar feature in Bengali: "... Bengali stress, though, is exceptional. It is non-phonemic, and, in the standard dialect, there is a strong tendency for it to be associated with word-initial syllables." ... [sect. 3.7.10, p. 227] Secondly, even in the Korobāri dialect, stress-placement indicates the contrast: stress falls on the first syllable of the main verb. audit.reasoning: (1) Every piece of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Wilde 2008 PDF/txt at the stated places (p. 32 sect. 2.5 with fn. 7; p. 227 sect. 3.7.10; case-marker 'does not carry stress' line; ch. 7 focus-stress line). (2) The classification rests on the best available description: a 559-pp reference grammar (published Helsinki PhD, 2008) that Toulmin 2009 independently calls the most thorough phonological analysis of any KRDS variety; its stress statement is hedged as preliminary but is supported inside the same work by stress-marked transcriptions ([ˈris], [ˈlihæn̪i], [ˈlilɪ]) and by the p. 227 verb-initial stress diagnostic, and externally by Toulmin 2009 p. 94 ('initial stress which characterises some KRDS lects... shared also with SCB').
